answer: As spring snow melts, the claimant logs the hour the first meltwater reaches their street drain, a time set by slope, shade and snow depth on their own hillside. A ridge above thaws first, an inlet below stays frozen longer, and a bridge over the stream marks where the water arrives last. A farm submitting one melt time for many identities collapses, since real melt times spread across the slope and cannot be guessed from a single point.
